Definition: from G4602; to keep silent (transitively or intransitively):--keep close (secret, silence), hold peace.
BiblicalUsage: Sigao means to keep silent, to hold one's peace, and it marks the moments when speech would do harm or when wonder stops the mouth. Tongues must keep silence in the church without an interpreter, Peter beckoned the household to hold their peace while he told of his escape, the council held their peace while James spoke, and the spies marvelled at Jesus' answer and held their peace.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe silence is sometimes the truest confession. I hold that the tongue that knows when to stop is the tongue God can use when it speaks.
